_comment: Real numbers from the evaluation run. Render these on the Results page. Do not edit values. Fields set to null are TODOs for the owner; show a 'pending' state, never an invented number.

eval_set.note: Balanced sample of the held-out test split plus every segment the detector got wrong. Rates describe generation quality on this sample, not population rates. Intervals are 95% Wilson.

arm_notes: Format failures for the prompted base are almost entirely em dashes, which a text filter would fix. The result shows consistency without post-processing and without a long style prompt.
The prompted base has fewer unsupported numbers because it copies numbers verbatim. The teacher and this model paraphrase and derive values such as ratios.
Verdict rows are not discriminating: every model was given the true label and followed it.

judge.method: Blind pairwise, A/B order randomized, 60 segments per pair, half anomalies and half nominal.
judge.bias_note: The judge is the same model family as the teacher, so it likely favours the teacher's writing style, which this model imitates. Read the first row as a clear but probably overstated edge, and the second as parity with the teacher.

detector_errors.summary: When the detector's flag was wrong, the report followed the wrong flag in every case. The model explains whatever flag it is given.

timing_lean.definition: The report's last sentence, the recommended next step, tells ops to check timestamps, packet logs, buffers, the downlink, or sampling clocks.
timing_lean.summary: The model recommends a timing-focused next step more often than its teacher. Greedy decoding amplifies the teacher's majority habit.

review_band.note: Chosen on the test split with only 19 detector errors, so the catch rates are optimistic. cross_validated is pending.

training.method: QLoRA (4-bit NF4), LoRA r=16 alpha=32 dropout=0.05 on all attention and MLP projections
